nice_guideline_used: CG181 / PH46 / NG28 (Metabolic syndrome components) and NG136 (Hypertension) and NG203 (CKD)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg PO once daily (titrate every 2 weeks to 5 mg, then 10 mg as tolerated)
medications.purpose: Control hypertension and provide renal protection
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136/NG203 recommend ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive, especially with renal risk
NICE NG136 allows CCB as add‑on when BP not at target on ACE‑I alone

medications.dose: 12.5 mg PO once daily (dose reduction from 25 mg)
medications.purpose: Assist BP control while minimizing metabolic side‑effects
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends thiazide diuretics; lower dose reduces glucose intolerance risk

medications.purpose: Reduce cardiovascular risk (≥10 % 10‑yr QRISK) and lower non‑HDL‑C >40 %
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 advise statin for adults with QRISK ≥10 % or multiple risk factors

medications.dose: 500 mg PO once daily with evening meal (titrate to 1000 mg BID as tolerated, max 2 g/day)
medications.purpose: Prevent progression from pre‑diabetes to type 2 diabetes and aid modest weight loss
medications.nice_justification: NICE PH38 & NG28 recommend metformin for high‑risk pre‑diabetes

medications.dose: 0.25 mg SC weekly (titrate to 1 mg weekly as tolerated)
medications.purpose: Weight management and additional glycaemic benefit in obesity (BMI ≥30)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 (2024 update) recommends GLP‑1 RA for obesity with BMI ≥30 when weight loss is a priority

medications.dose: 5 mg/ML IM injection (as per haematology protocol)
medications.duration: Continue per protocol (e.g., monthly for 3 months then maintenance)
medications.nice_justification: NICE haematology guidance for B12‑deficiency anaemia

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect; risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury, especially if volume depleted
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium and creatinine 1–2 weeks after initiation or dose change; ensure adequate hydration

interactions_checked.interaction: Generally safe; modest increase in amlodipine levels not clinically significant
interactions_checked.action: No dose adjustment needed; monitor blood pressure

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma concentrations (~1.5‑fold), raising myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin 20 mg (lower than 40 mg) and monitor CK if muscle symptoms develop

interactions_checked.interaction: Metformin may reduce vitamin B12 levels, potentially worsening anaemia
interactions_checked.action: Continue B12 supplementation and check serum B12 annually

interactions_checked.interaction: Thiazide diuretics can raise glucose; metformin counteracts this effect

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated if eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73 m² (risk of lactic acidosis)
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR 30‑45, start at 500 mg daily with dose adjustment; if <30, consider DPP‑4 inhibitor

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated in patients with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN‑2
contraindications.alternative: Consider orlistat 120 mg TDS if GLP‑1 RA contraindicated

treatment_summary: Start ramipril and reduce hydrochlorothiazide to 12.5 mg to optimise blood pressure while limiting metabolic side‑effects. Continue amlodipine as add‑on. Initiate atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for cardiovascular risk reduction. Begin metformin MR 500 mg daily (titrating to 2 g) to prevent diabetes progression, with monitoring of renal function. Offer semaglutide for weight loss if no contraindications. Continue vitamin B12 injections for anaemia. All recommendations follow NICE CG181/PH46/NG28 for metabolic syndrome, NG136 for hypertension, and NG203 for renal protection. Baseline labs (eGFR, electrolytes, LFTs, lipids, glucose) and QRISK calculation are required before implementation, with regular monitoring as outlined.
